source: Progressive Context Disclosure for Long-Context Agents
summary: Loading a compact index (~800 tokens) first and fetching only relevant context chunks on demand approaches near-100% retrieval efficiency while cutting token costs significantly. A hierarchical variant maps directly onto AgentForge's promptRenderer and ProcessRunner architecture.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly implementable as index-first prompt protocol over stdin/stdout; no model changes required

source: RL for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems through Orchestration Traces
summary: Logging orchestration decisions (when to spawn, delegate, aggregate, stop) in a standardized replayable JSON schema creates a training corpus for future orchestration policy optimization via RL, with 84 tagged entries and a minimal schema for replayable traces.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — AgentForge's state machine already makes the five orchestration decisions described; additive JSON logging at advanceState() creates RL training data with zero architecture change

source: AgentLTL: Formal Specification and Compliance Measurement for LLM Agent Evaluation
summary: First-Order LTL language for expressing procedural compliance rules over agent execution traces with online prefix-checking (harnessing) mode that blocks tool calls violating specifications before execution; +38pp accuracy and +17.5pp compliance gains.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — orchestration harness verification (not model verification) is exactly AgentForge's layer; four default policies map directly to existing policyEngine allowedPaths constraints and the subprocess model

source: Mem-alpha: Learning Memory Construction via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Frames memory update as a sequential MDP and uses Group-Relative PPO to train an agent to decide what to store and how to structure it, achieving lower memory footprint with better downstream performance than static baselines.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — maps to AgentForge's lack of cross-run memory, but too close to existing HID-161/HID-145/HID-170 issues which already cover episodic memory

source: MemexRL: Scaling Long-Horizon LLM Agents via Indexed Experience Memory
summary: Two-tier architecture: compact working context of structured summaries plus stable indices pointing into full-fidelity external database. Uses reward shaping to train agent to decide what to summarize and archive. Lifts ALFWorld success from 24% to 86%.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — but already subsumed by existing HID-161, HID-145, HID-131 memory issues in AgentForge backlog

source: MemPro: Agentic Memory Systems as Evolvable Programs
summary: Treats the memory construction-retrieval pipeline as a versioned evolvable program with failure-mode-guided edit-debug refinement. Maintains a version tree of runnable pipeline implementations. Outperforms static baselines on LongMemEval.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — novel 'pipeline as code' model but requires memory system infrastructure not yet present; too complex given 7+ memory issues already in backlog

source: RecMem: Recurrence-based Memory Consolidation (ACL 2026)
summary: Only calls LLM for memory consolidation when sustained recurrence is observed in semantically similar interactions; lightweight embedding handles routine storage. Cuts memory construction token cost by up to 87%.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — cost optimization for memory management is excellent but requires a memory system to exist first; pre-requisite issues (HID-161/170) not yet implemented

source: Adaptive Memory Structures for LLM Agents
summary: Benchmarks five memory architectures and derives selection heuristics based on task horizon and retrieval latency budget. Useful for choosing which memory approach to implement first.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — good reference for choosing among memory approaches when implementing HID-161/HID-170; not an independent enhancement

source: Hermes Agent: Skill-Saving Self-Improvement Loop (Nous Research)
summary: After any task with 5+ tool calls, a background fork summarizes trajectory into a Markdown skill file with YAML frontmatter. Foreground task is never blocked. Skill files become durable procedural memory without human intervention.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — background-fork pattern is implementable alongside subprocess model, but too close to existing HID-165 (inject trace-derived skill hints) and HID-164 (failure summaries in prompts)

source: The Kitchen Loop: User-Spec-Driven Development for Self-Evolving Codebase
summary: Six-phase autonomous improvement cycle (Backlog → Ideate → Triage → Execute → Polish → Regress) with synthetic 'As a User x1000' exerciser, Unbeatable Tests, and Drift Control auto-pause. Validated over 285+ iterations producing 1,094 merged PRs with zero regressions.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Drift Control auto-pause concept is novel, but the full cycle is too large in scope for a 1-2 sprint issue; would require fundamental changes to orchestration lifecycle

source: Regimes: Auditable Held-Out-Gated Improvement Loop (Yohei Nakajima)
summary: Event-sourced agent runtime where every repair must pass sequential gates (static checks, sandbox execution, in-sample eval, held-out validation) before promotion. From BabyAGI author; also at github.com/yoheinakajima/regimes.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — sequential gate promotion for repairs is distinct from existing HID-144/HID-168; strong candidate but selected AgentLTL (HID-173) over this due to higher novelty score

source: SPORK: Self-Speculative Forking to Accelerate Agentic LLM Inference
summary: Exploits LLM's ability to predict its own upcoming tool call name (74.6-99.6% accuracy) by probing internal states, forking tool dispatch early to overlap execution with remaining chain-of-thought decode. Cuts Qwen3-32B GAIA P95 latency 18%.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — thin controller over standard API is attractive, but for CLI subprocess model the internal state probing is not directly accessible; also close to HID-101 (speculative implementation)

source: B-PASTE: Beam-Aware Pattern-Guided Speculative Execution
summary: Extends single-tool speculative execution to bounded branch hypotheses with a beam ranked by expected critical-path reduction. Models co-run interference and downstream unlock value. Up to 1.4x speedup in edge-class environments.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — beam ranking by downstream unlock value is compelling but requires parallel execution infrastructure not yet in AgentForge; too close to HID-101

source: Cost-Aware Speculative Execution: Five-Dimension Method
summary: Models agent workflow as DAG and defines five dimensions for speculative cost accounting: prediction accuracy, rollback cost, downstream dependency depth, token billing asymmetry, and wall-clock latency. Shows naive speculation can increase cost even when reducing latency.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — five-dimension cost model is directly applicable for choosing where to introduce speculation; but duplicates coverage of HID-101 and HID-143 budget allocation

source: ProRL Agent: Rollout-as-a-Service for RL Training (NVIDIA NeMo Gym)
summary: Decouples multi-turn agentic rollout orchestration from RL training loop via HTTP service with async three-stage assembly line: INIT (sandbox containers), RUN (trajectory collection), EVAL (reward scoring). Open-sourced as NeMo Gym.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — mirrors AgentForge's CLI subprocess model; blueprint for RL training signal but requires training infrastructure not in scope for 1-2 sprint issue

source: ARPO: Agentic Reinforced Policy Optimization (ICLR 2026)
summary: Entropy-based adaptive rollout that branches sampling at high-entropy tool-call rounds with step-level advantage attribution. Achieves superior performance across 13 benchmarks using half the tool-use budget of trajectory-level RL algorithms.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — step-level advantage attribution reduces credit-assignment noise in long sequences; complementary to ProRL but requires RL training infrastructure

source: TAO-RL: Tool-Aware Optimization with Entropy Guidance
summary: Filters training trajectories by discarding those where all tool invocations fail, then adds entropy bonuses at post-tool-call tokens to encourage diverse reasoning paths. Complementary to ARPO.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — requires RL training pipeline; no direct implementation path without first building ProRL infrastructure

source: RL for LLM Agent Planning: Process Without Answers
summary: Trains planning policy using process-level reward even when final answer correctness is unavailable, enabling RL in domains where tools don't return verifiable ground-truth signals.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — addresses exactly AgentForge's problem where CLI tools may not produce verifiable success signals; too early without training infrastructure

source: Graceful Degradation Patterns in AI Agent Systems (Zylos Research)
summary: Documents layered resilience patterns: circuit breakers, fallback chains, bulkheads, self-healing state machines. Distinguishes transient errors worth retrying from permanent errors that should not be.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — but already fully covered by HID-162 (stage-aware retry with circuit breaker), HID-156 (exponential-backoff retry), HID-141 (circuit breaker)

source: BATS: Budget-Aware Tool-Use Enables Effective Agent Scaling
summary: Dynamically adapts planning and verification based on remaining token and tool-call budget, deciding whether to dig deeper or pivot at each step. Formalizes unified cost metric for tokens plus tool invocations.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — already covered by HID-169 (budget-aware dynamic stage timeouts) and HID-129 (token-budget-aware adaptive granularity)

source: BAAR: Budget-Aware Agentic Routing via Boundary-Guided Training
summary: Formulates dynamic model routing for agentic workflows as sequential decision process, training lightweight router to switch between cheap and expensive models based on remaining budget. Boundary-guided training near capability threshold.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — already covered by HID-160 (stage-aware dynamic model router) and HID-157 (stage-adaptive model routing)

source: Karpathy Agentic Engineering Framework (Sequoia Ascent 2026)
summary: Five core agentic engineering skills: spec design, diff review, eval design, security oversight, quality taste. Shift from operating code to operating knowledge with LLMs maintaining structured Markdown wikis through knowledge linting.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — conceptual framework valuable for understanding AgentForge's design principles; eval design maps to RL corpus work (HID-172) but not independently actionable

source: CASTER: Context-Aware Strategy for Task Efficient Routing
summary: Identifies task complexity upfront using context signals and routes to appropriately capable model, bypassing iterative trial-and-error escalation. Minimizes cost by avoiding wasteful strong-model calls on simple tasks.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — already covered by HID-160 (stage-aware dynamic model router with task-complexity scoring) and HID-113 (task-complexity-driven per-stage model routing)

source: VoltAgent/awesome-ai-agent-papers (2026 curated collection)
summary: Curated living index of AI agent research papers released in 2026 with tagged categories covering memory, evaluation, workflows, and autonomous systems. Discovery surface for niche low-star papers.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low as a direct source — high as a discovery tool for future runs; no specific implementable enhancement itself

source: Temporal Workflow Streams (Replay 2026 public preview)
summary: Durable streaming abstraction built on Temporal's Signal and Update primitives. Offset-addressed event channel that survives worker restarts. AI agents can stream status and output to UI in real time with no Redis or custom SSE server. TypeScript SDK in pre-release.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — TypeScript SDK matches tech stack; durable streaming would address lack of incremental output visibility; TypeScript SDK still in pre-release, revisit when stable

source: SKILL.md Standard and Capability Mismatch Crisis (arXiv:2605.11418)
summary: Emerging standard for declaring agent skills via SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter. Scanning 49,943 skills found 80% had at least one mismatch between declared capabilities and actual behavior. 250,706 total behavioral deviations.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — capability declaration pre-assignment checking is novel; complex to implement for CLI agents that don't expose SKILL.md; may require wrapping each agent variant with declaration files

source: SkillResolve-Bench: Same-Capability Ambiguity in Skill Retrieval
summary: Benchmarks problem of multiple skills claiming the same capability but behaving differently. Proposes resolution approaches for agents to pick the right skill when several appear equivalent.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge has fixed agent-to-stage mapping so skill selection ambiguity is not currently a problem; relevant if dynamic routing is implemented later

source: JFrog Agent Skills Registry
summary: Extends JFrog artifact management to agent skills with versioning, dependency scanning, and admission controls at publish time. Commercial product treating skills like npm packages with known CVEs.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — commercial product; not directly usable without adopting JFrog platform; AgentForge uses fixed CLI agents not a skill marketplace

source: SAGE-HLS: Syntax-Aware AST-Guided LLM Code Generation
summary: Fine-tunes Qwen-Coder 7B on 16.7K HLS C/C++ codes paired with ASTs. Code generation is guided by AST structure at inference time. Near 100% synthesizability and 75% functional correctness vs lower baseline rates.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — injecting TypeScript AST (via ts-morph) as structured context before implementation is an interesting direction; domain-specific to HLS currently, not general TypeScript

source: SemanticALLI: Caching Reasoning Stages Not Just Responses
summary: Caches intermediate structured representations as first-class artifacts rather than final LLM responses. Analytic Intent Resolution stage cached hits rise from 38.7% to 83.1%, bypassing 4,023 LLM calls with 2.66ms median lookup.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — stage-level caching could reduce token costs substantially; complex to implement for CLI agents that don't decompose into discrete sub-stages internally

source: TVCACHE: Stateful Tool-Value Cache
summary: State-aware caching using longest-prefix tree matching for tool call sequences: a cache hit is valid only when the agent's full tool history matches a previously executed sequence. Achieved 70% hit rate and 6.9x reduction in tool call execution time.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — genuinely novel state-aware caching not in any OSS framework; complex to implement for CLI subprocess model where tool calls are inside the subprocess; strong candidate for future run

source: Agentic Plan Caching (arXiv:2506.14852)
summary: Caches plan templates extracted from completed agent executions and adapts them to new queries using a lightweight model. Designed for task-level (not query-level) caching as existing caching is built for chatbots.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — task-level plan template reuse is interesting; somewhat covered by HID-155 (prompt cache prefix reuse) at a different layer

source: agent-replay: TypeScript SQLite Fork-from-Checkpoint Replay
summary: 6-star TypeScript CLI for time-travel debugging: step-by-step replay, side-by-side trace diff, fork at any checkpoint to re-run without re-paying for prior LLM calls, AI-powered hallucination evaluation, export to golden CI datasets.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — TypeScript-native, directly usable; similar to HID-152 (run fork-and-replay API) which already covers this area; fork-from-checkpoint is the novel addition over HID-152

source: Replayable Agent Runtimes via Event Sourcing (Zylos Research)
summary: Proposes event-sourced execution as foundation: every agent action is an immutable event appended to a log; current state derived by replaying the log. Enables parameter substitution at replay time.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — complementary to HID-152 and agent-replay; event-sourcing is a good architectural pattern but not a distinct new issue given existing coverage

source: Knowledge-Based Zero-Replay Debugging (arXiv:2606.14805)
summary: Instead of replaying traces, uses knowledge distilled from traces to debug without re-running. Contrasts with full deterministic replay on cost and scalability for long multi-agent runs.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — interesting counterpoint to replay approaches but primarily relevant once a memory system is implemented

source: ToolLoad-Bench: Cognitive Load Framework for Tool-Using Agents (AAAI 2026)
summary: Decomposes task complexity into Intrinsic Load (Tool Interaction Graph: tools needed and dependency order) and Extraneous Load (presentation ambiguity). Reveals distinct performance cliffs as cognitive load increases, enabling precise model capability boundary mapping.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — pre-task complexity estimation via TIG before subprocess spawn is genuinely novel approach; covered at a coarser level by HID-128 and HID-169 but TIG-based routing is more precise

source: Cognitive Load-Aware Inference: Attention Entropy as Proxy (arXiv:2507.00653)
summary: Proposes Attention Entropy as a proxy for cognitive load during inference: higher entropy in attention distribution correlates with higher cognitive load. Can be measured to trigger compute allocation decisions during generation.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — requires access to model attention weights which are not exposed by Claude Code or Codex CLI subprocesses; not implementable without model internals access

source: ICSE 2026 NIER: Towards Verifiably Safe Tool Use for LLM Agents
summary: Proposes formal verification of the agentic framework that mediates between LLM and external state, rather than trying to verify the LLM itself. Verifying the orchestration harness formally shows boundary-event safety for every typed action.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly supports HID-173 AgentLTL implementation; included as companion citation in that issue

source: MANTRA: SMT-Validated Compliance Benchmarks for Tool-Using Agents
summary: Uses SMT solvers to synthesize test cases that exercise compliance requirements for tool-using agents, producing formally validated benchmarks. Complementary to AgentLTL for test generation.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — useful for testing the policies defined in HID-173 but not a standalone enhancement; tool for benchmark generation not a runtime feature

source: Claude Agent SDK Dynamic Workflows and Planner-Generator-Evaluator Pattern
summary: Anthropic shipped Dynamic Workflows, Subagents, and Agent Teams in May 2026. Production pattern: Planner/Generator/Evaluator with structured artifact handoffs and 5-15 critique-and-refine cycles between agents.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — artifact-handoff pattern is directly applicable; but AgentForge already uses typed JSON structured output between stages, which IS the artifact-handoff pattern; no new issue needed

source: claude-pm: Multi-Subprocess Claude Orchestration (bobmatnyc/claude-pm)
summary: AI-driven project management where orchestrator Claude session reads task queue, decides next action, invokes subprocess Claude instances for each worker unit, and updates the queue with results.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — similar orchestration model to AgentForge; no specific innovation beyond what AgentForge already does with state machine

source: Deterministic Multi-Agent Orchestration via Artifact Handoff (alexop.dev)
summary: Using Claude Code --output-format json and structured handoff artifacts to build deterministic orchestration flows where routing logic is in code not in the model. Each subprocess produces typed JSON artifact; orchestrator routes; next subprocess gets clean structured input.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge already implements this pattern via BEGIN_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT/END_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT; no new enhancement identified

source: confidence-escalation: Multi-Signal Composite Escalation Middleware
summary: Combines logprobs, verbalized confidence, and tool risk assessment into composite escalation score with five pluggable handlers: Human-in-Loop, Model Upgrade, Tool Restriction, Compliance Logging, Abort. Framework-agnostic Python middleware.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — multi-signal composite (verbalized confidence + tool risk + retry count) is adaptable to subprocess JSON output parsing without logprob access; strong candidate for future run

source: AI Agents Need Escalation Contracts Not Just Human Oversight (VKTR)
summary: Machine-readable escalation contracts specifying conditions (confidence drop, action type, data sensitivity, cost of being wrong) rather than a single threshold. Contract defines what triggers escalation, what context is packaged, and what human must do before agent resumes.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — HumanClarificationNeeded state already exists; escalation contracts would formalize trigger conditions; covered at a basic level by existing issue HID-149

source: AWS Well-Architected Agentic AI Lens: Human Escalation Best Practices
summary: Formalizes multi-agent handoff procedures with human-in-the-loop escalation as well-architected best practice. Separates agent-to-agent triggers from agent-to-human triggers.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — vendor guidance documentation; no specific novel technical contribution beyond what AgentForge's existing HumanClarificationNeeded state already provides

source: Autonomous Event-Driven Multi-Agent Orchestration for Enterprise AI (arXiv:2606.20058)
summary: Formal paper on event-driven multi-agent architectures. Key finding: event-driven architectures reduce system latency by 70-90% versus polling. Three-component model: Event Producers, Event Bus, Event Consumers subscribed to event types.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge already uses Linear webhooks as event-driven triggers; the paper validates the approach but suggests broader event types (CI events, file system changes) not yet consumed

source: Inngest: Durable Event Consumption Platform for AI Agents
summary: Event-driven queue and workflow platform for serverless applications. Agents define event-driven functions triggering on matching events. Durable consumption: if agent function fails mid-execution, event is not lost and function re-executes from checkpoint.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — durable event consumption is valuable; but Inngest is a commercial platform requiring platform migration; AgentForge already has Fastify webhook handlers

source: Webhook-Driven Agent Architecture Guide for Fastify 2026
summary: Documents production failure modes in webhook-driven agent architectures: idempotency, replay ordering, exactly-once delivery. Describes patterns for building Fastify HTTP webhook handlers that trigger agent processes correctly.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge already implements Fastify webhooks for Linear events; idempotency already handled by state machine; no new enhancement identified
